newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan did not discuss forex levels with U.S. -MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan did not discuss forex levels with U.S. -MOF.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday that he did not discuss specific currency levels with U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers during talks on the sidelines of the meeting of the "Six Markets" group in Tokyo last week.
Mitsuzuka, speaking at a key parliamentary committee meeting, made the comments to clarify what he said earlier about a dollar rise of above 125 yen would cause trade friction with the United States.
He had also said that Summers told him that the United States was worried that Japan's growing trade surplus could cause trade or economic friction.

The finance minister, clarifying his earlier comments, said that the currency level was around 125 yen to the dollar at the time before the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations' meeting on February 8.
"I just wanted to state the fact that the yen fell close to 125 (against the dollar). I did not speak with the U.S. deputy treasury secretary on specific currency levels," he said.
